correctness.rationale: Assessed the corrected /workspace/repairs/4/RESULT.md. The frozen phrase ‘open simplex’ taken literally is incorrect: even the apex is in F_G minus M_G. The replacement states precisely that only the base facet is removed. Balinski’s half-integral support description leaves only the all-half rim as a fractional vertex because every other edge meets the rim. For cyclic shift P of odd order, (I+P)^(−1)=(1/2)Σ_{r=0}^{n−1}(−P)^r and |det(I+P)|=2. In mixed degree-slack and leaf coordinates the defect is all nonnegative vectors of total j<1, since each inverse rim coordinate is ≥(1−j)/2; equality j=1 gives the base. Unit base vectors leave one rim vertex unmatched or match that vertex to its designated leaf. Every new clipped vertex is on that integral base, and every old retained vertex is integral, so the clipped polytope is exactly M_G. The determinant gives volume 1/(2d!). At dilation k, summing the inverse equations gives right-hand side total nk−j. The cycle matrix has image exactly the even-sum sublattice by containment and index two. Stars and bars on the surviving j<k of parity k yields the asserted count (in particular Δ(0)=Δ(1)=0, Δ(2)=1 and Δ(3)=d). The single pole at −1 gives 2^(−d−1)(−1)^k, which cannot cancel a lattice Ehrhart polynomial. The repair preserves the quantitative formulas and scope. The frozen checker and verification notes were read, not executed: enumeration counts strict rim-inequality violations for 47 finite cases; the proof, not the enumeration, identifies the matching hull in general.

value.rationale: The full defect answers how a natural fractional relaxation differs from its matching hull at every lattice dilation. It distinguishes exact period from the denominator-two upper bound, and distinguishes the full lattice correction from the previously known bare volume or the alternating coefficient alone. The leaf-slack characterization explains why arbitrary attachment patterns with the same edge count give the very same count despite changing the two polytopes. The assessment is for direct leaves only and does not assign novelty to the classical cut or lattice counting in isolation.
